citations.B1: Race condition on read-modify-write of `counts[user_id]` across threads
citations.B3: use a per-key lock or an atomic increment (e.g. `threading.Lock`, or an atomic counter/Redis INCR)
citations.B4: No time window — once `limit` is hit, user is blocked forever, not per-minute/hour
citations.B5: Unbounded memory growth — `counts` never evicts entries
citations.B6: State is process-local, so each worker enforces its own limit → effective limit is `limit * num_workers`
citations.B7: No input validation on `user_id`/`limit` — malicious or malformed `user_id` (None, huge string) still gets an entry — validate/sanitize before use.
